title: Quiesce-and-roll-forward: orchestrated VPC runtime upgrade with fast rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a coordinated VPC private-runtime upgrade pattern that minimizes customer-facing interruptions by putting nodes into a 'quiesce' state, snapshotting volatile runtime state, performing a fast rolling upgrade (roll-forward), and supporting sub-5min rollback to the prior runtime when health thresholds fail. This ticket ties Terraform/IaC hooks, the operator orchestration, runtime drain semantics, KV cache snapshot/restore, and health-check gating into a single pipeline that can be exercised in staging and safely promoted to production clusters.
acceptance_criteria: Can trigger a staged upgrade from the operator that marks a pool as quiesced and prevents new sessions from landing
KV cache snapshot completes and is uploaded to S3 before upgrade proceeds for >95% of primed tenants
Rolling upgrade proceeds without breaking existing in-flight requests for <99th percentile latency increase of 15%
Automated rollback can be initiated by the operator within 5 minutes and restores previous runtime and KV snapshot with verified health checks
Terraform modules expose toggle flags for quiesce-timeout, snapshot-s3-bucket, health-check-quorum and rollback-policy
Runbook steps and a Datadog/CloudWatch dashboard for the rollout are linked and validated in a dry-run in staging
implementation_notes: Add a new operator annotation `redwood.io/quiesce-mode=true|false` to control node acceptance of new workloads
Introduce a two-phase drain: soft drain (stop accepting new sessions) then hard drain after KV snapshot and active lease timeout
KV snapshot uses incremental delta snapshots to reduce pause time; snapshot agent uploads to customer-specific S3 path with encryption headers
Terraform module `redwood_private_runtime` will add lifecycle hooks: pre_upgrade (health preflight), pause (set quiesce), snapshot, upgrade, post_upgrade (health quorum check), rollback-trigger
Health gating uses a quorum of node-level health probes + end-to-end synthetic checks against the model route; thresholds defined in Terraform variable `health_check_threshold`
Rollback path restores previous container image tag, restores KV snapshot, and executes smoke tests before re-opening traffic
Add optimistic circuit-breaker that routes a small percentage of traffic to the newly upgraded nodes during canary to detect regressions quickly
Instrument request traces to capture priming hits/misses pre and post upgrade to detect regression in cache priming
notes: Tradeoffs considered: full cold restart vs quiesce+snapshot; quiesce reduces latency spikes but requires reliable snapshot/restore path
We rejected a monolithic global lock to avoid cross-tenant blast radius; adopted per-pool/quorum approach
Rollback speed relies on snapshot restore speed; investing in incremental delta snapshots reduces restore time but slightly increases complexity
Operator/API change required: expose `force-rollback` with explicit audit trail and two-step confirmation for production
testing_plan: Stage dry-run against staging clusters with synthetic traffic generator that mimics customer token distribution
Chaos tests: simulate snapshot upload failure, half-node flapping, and slow disk during restore
Load test to validate latency SLOs with KV snapshot/restore in the loop
Manual tabletop with on-call and SRE to run rollback scenario and measure RTO
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature flags in staging cluster for operator and Terraform modules
2) Run quiesce+snapshot dry-run on a single tenant pool (low-traffic) and validate snapshots
3) Canary: upgrade 5% of pools with optimistic circuit-breaker for 10 minutes
4) Promote to 30% pools with 30-minute observation window and health gating
5) Full roll-forward after automated health gates pass for 6 hours
6) If any gate fails, operator triggers staged rollback for affected pools only and notifies runbook flow
